# Caption style guide (what makes captions look edited, not auto-generated)

**Typography**
- Two faces only: condensed caps (Anton) for headline + tags; geometric bold (Montserrat ExtraBold) for subtitles.
- Headline: caps, tight leading (0.98), balanced line lengths, as big as fits 960 px — never a ragged last word.
- Subtitles: sentence case, 56 px, ≤ 26 characters per line, ≤ 2 lines, balanced; break after commas, never before
  a one-word last line.
- One accent colour for emphasis (orange on the white page, yellow on dark) — at most one word per line.

**Placement — fixed homes, never wandering**
- Headline: top, centred, 64 px from the top edge, inside the safe area.
- Tags: top strip (or right under the headline). Centred. One at a time.
- Subtitles: lower third, centred, above the narrator's head; nothing else lives there.
- Keep clear of the platform UI: nothing important below y≈85% or within 60 px of the sides.

**Motion — quiet and consistent**
- Headline lines slide up out of a mask with a 3-frame stagger, then hold; it lifts away when the hook ends.
- Tags wipe in from the left on their word, hold ~1.8 s, wipe out to the right.
- Subtitles rise 10 px and fade in over 5 frames; they cut cleanly to the next phrase. No bounce, no tilt, no shake.

**Timing**
- Each subtitle phrase ≥ 0.8 s on screen; tags ≥ 1.2 s; headline ≥ the whole hook line.
- Text lands with the word that says it — never before the narrator gets there.

**Restraint**
- If a word is already big on the board, don't tag it.
- Fewer, better: a tag every few seconds reads as design; a tag every line reads as noise.
